subject.title: [Feature]: Auto-discovery of agent configurations from external workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw add core trusted external-workspace agent-config discovery, or keep agent registration explicit and improve the existing CLI/RPC management path instead?
rationale: The request adds a new public config surface, filesystem scanning, trust boundaries, and live routing semantics; those product and security choices cannot be safely made by cleanup automation.

options.title: Keep Explicit Registration
options.body: Continue using `agents.list`, `$include`, `openclaw agents add`, and `agents.create/update/delete`, and improve batch or zero-restart operator tooling without adding core glob discovery.

options.title: Design Trusted Discovery
options.body: Define a core discovery contract with trusted roots, allowed file names, validation, precedence, reload behavior, agentDir/session isolation, and security proof before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Zero-Restart Management
options.body: First improve explicit runtime registration and binding reload semantics, then revisit whether external workspace glob discovery belongs in core.

recommendation.title: Keep Explicit Registration
recommendation.body: Continue using `agents.list`, `$include`, `openclaw agents add`, and `agents.create/update/delete`, and improve batch or zero-restart operator tooling without adding core glob discovery.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest history signal for the model-visible `agents_list` and adjacent multi-agent discovery boundary.
